content:
Apple TV currently boasts a strong lineup of shows, with flagship titles including "Slow Horses," "Ted Lasso," "Dark Matter," and the brand-new comedy "Brothers" starring Matthew McConaughey. But there's plenty more to look forward to—here's everything premiering on Apple TV in October.

The Last First: Winter K2

  • Date: October 2
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Documentary

"The Last First: Winter K2," directed by Amir Bar-Lev, tells a complex, thrilling, and moving story that unravels the extreme mountaineering industry and how its culture has evolved. Centered on a 2021 expedition, it follows Icelandic mountaineer John Snorri Sigurjónsson and the Pakistani father-and-son team Ali and Sajid Sadpara, who hope to become the first people to summit K2 in winter—the most brutal season on the mountain. These skilled climbers quickly discover that they're sharing the route with social media climber-influencers and their film crews, clients of commercial expeditions, and Nepali climbing celebrity Nims and his team of Sherpas. "The Last First: Winter K2" takes viewers up to K2's frozen peaks and into the unpredictable weather, revealing an unexpected, layered story—one of strategy and determination, class and hierarchy, money and power—all unfolding in life-or-death situations.

The Sisters Grimm (Season 2)

  • Date: October 2
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Kids & Family

Two orphaned sisters live in a town filled with fairy tale and fantasy characters, confronting heroes and villains head-on while investigating the mystery of their parents' disappearance. "The Sisters Grimm" blends mystery, fantasy, and adventure to deliver meaningful messages for viewers of all ages.

Small Prophets

  • Date: October 7
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Comedy

"Small Prophets" is a comedy about eccentric Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley). Ever since his beloved Clea vanished seven years ago, he's been living a quiet life—working at a hardware store, visiting his dad Brian (Sir Michael Palin), and hoping that one day Clea will return. One day, Brian shares an ancient recipe whose ingredients include rainwater, horse manure, and a touch of alchemy. Though skeptical, Michael takes the recipe and decides to try making a "homunculus"—a magical spirit that can predict the future—hoping to find the answer he wants most: "Do I still have a chance of seeing Clea again?"

Matchbox The Movie

  • Date: October 9
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Action

"Matchbox The Movie," inspired by the classic Mattel toy, is an action-packed adventure that spans the globe. The story follows a group of childhood friends whose lives are upended when CIA undercover agent Sean (John Cena)—their long-lost big brother figure—suddenly returns to the small town where they grew up, inadvertently pulling them into a high-stakes, globe-trotting race to save the world.

Tenzing

  • Date: October 16
  • Type: Film
  • Category: Drama

"Tenzing" is based on the true story of the lesser-known Genden Phuntsok. A gifted Himalayan mountaineer, he joined New Zealand climber Edmund Hillary (Tom Hiddleston) to become one of the first people to reach the summit of Everest. Encouraged by his wife Dawa (Thinley Lhamo) and supported by expedition secretary Jill Henderson (Caitríona Balfe), Genden works to convince Colonel John Hunt (Willem Dafoe) that he belongs as a member of the British climbing team—not merely as a "porter" serving them. While Western climbers see "Everest" as a peak to be conquered, Genden reverently calls "Chomolungma" a sacred mother goddess. The journey that follows is fraught with tension over background, class, and personal ambition, as well as constant danger on the mountain. But at the top of the world, empire, status, and ambition fall away, leaving only two outsiders bound by mutual respect and trust—for Genden, the fulfillment of a lifelong dream and spiritual calling.

Where's Wanda? (Season 2)

  • Date: October 21
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Dark Comedy

Apple's first German-language series, "Where's Wanda?" is a dark comedy about parents Dedo and Carlotta Klatt, who are desperate to find their seventeen-year-old daughter Wanda, who vanished without warning months ago. After the police investigation turns up nothing, the family takes matters into their own hands and, with the help of their tech-savvy son Ole, acquires surveillance equipment. Posing as utility company workers, they install listening devices on the neighbours—eventually expanding to half the neighbourhood—and discover that behind closed doors, none of the neighbours are what they seem.

Nocturne

  • Date: October 30
  • Type: Series
  • Category: Crime Drama

The series follows former soldier turned homicide detective Jonah Lynn (Liev Schreiber), who's grown tired of chasing cases on the busy streets of Philadelphia and moves to a small town in western Pennsylvania, hoping for a quieter life. But when the town and his family are targeted by cunning serial killer Jurek Walter (Graham), Jonah must protect everything he holds dear. With the search for Jurek's final missing victim forcing Jonah to send his goddaughter—FBI agent Saga Bauer (Beetz)—to confront Jurek head-on, how far will Jonah ultimately go?

New Episodes: "Slow Horses," "Brothers," and More

Apple TV will also roll out new episodes of several currently airing series throughout October, including:

  • "Ted Lasso": The Jason Sudeikis-led comedy, with new episodes airing through October 7.
  • "Last Seen": A crime-mystery series, with new episodes airing through October 7.
  • "Slow Horses": The acclaimed British spy thriller, with new episodes airing through October 21.
  • "Dark Matter": The sci-fi series starring Joel Edgerton, with new episodes airing through October 30.
  • "Brothers": The comedy starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, with new episodes airing through November 4.

Which of Apple TV's October releases are you planning to watch? Share with us in the comments.

Apple TV costs USD 14.99 per month, and you can also get a discount through an Apple One bundle.
